title: Land the enterprise deal
summary: Type II and the pen test in hand, status page live, NDA signed, the questionnaire cleared, the contract closed.

parts.title: Complete SOC 2 Type II
parts.guidance: Determine which assurance evidence the prospect actually requires and whether the company's existing report covers the relevant service and period. Use the Type II workflow to coordinate auditor scope, evidence and remediation where work remains. Share the issued report under the applicable access terms and identify the systems, periods and requested assurances it does not cover.

parts.title: Run the annual penetration test
parts.guidance: Agree the penetration-test scope around the systems relevant to the enterprise customer's review, including authorization and testing constraints. Follow the testing workflow through findings, remediation and any retest. Prepare the report or customer-safe summary with the status of each material finding, including remediation and any retest result.

parts.title: Publish a status page & SLA
parts.guidance: Match service-status reporting and proposed commitments to the product's actual operational capabilities. Use the status-page and SLA workflow to define incident ownership, audience and the information that can be published. Test the communication path and retain approved commitments so the contract team does not promise response or availability terms operations cannot support.

parts.title: Send NDA
parts.guidance: Identify the parties, purpose and information expected to be shared in the enterprise evaluation. Use the NDA workflow to review scope, exceptions, term and signing authority before execution. Store the signed agreement and communicate its practical sharing constraints to the sales and security teams before releasing restricted diligence material.

parts.title: Answer a security questionnaire
parts.guidance: Assemble answers from current policies, implemented controls and supporting evidence, using the customer's questionnaire version. Route unknown or qualified answers to the responsible security or product owner. Have an authorized reviewer approve the completed response and attachments before submission, retaining the version sent so later contract commitments remain consistent with the representations made.

parts.title: Negotiate SaaS agreement
parts.guidance: Negotiate the SaaS agreement using the approved commercial offer, security representations and operational commitments. Identify deviations in liability, data handling, service levels and termination for the proper decision-makers. Obtain authorized legal and business approval before signature, then hand the executed terms and implementation obligations to billing, support and delivery owners.
